newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel advances plan to put Jews in Arab Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Israel advances plan to put Jews in Arab Jerusalem.

text.p: An Israeli planning commission on Tuesday approved the building of 132 housing units for Jews in the heart of an Arab East Jerusalem neighbourhood in a move bound to infuriate Palestinians.
"Yes, that's correct," an interior ministry spokeswoman said when asked to confirm a radio report. The plan will not be final until it is signed by Interior Minister Eliahu Suissa.

Palestinians and officials in Israel's former government -- which rejected the plan -- have warned that the plan to build Jewish housing in East Jerusalem's Ras al-Amud neighbourhood could provoke a violent outburst if implemented.

Israel's opening of an entrance to a tunnel near Moslem sites in Jerusalem in September, a move also rejected by the previous administration, touched off clashes in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.

The status of East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war along with the rest of the West Bank, is up for negotiations in final status peace talks which have yet to resume under Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who took office in June.

There are now some 160,000 Jews living in East Jerusalem amidst and around 155,000 Palestinians. The PLO wants East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future Palestinian state. Israel regards the city as part of its "eternal" capital.

While all Israeli governments have built housing for Jews in the eastern part of the city since 1967 to reinforce its claim to the area, the previous government refrained from settling Jews in the heart of existing Arab neighbourhoods.
